name: Missive
description: Missive is a collaborative inbox and team communication product combining email and other channels with conversations, internal comments, drafts, tasks, assignments, labels, and contacts.
agentUseSummary: Missive cannot currently be connected because its official REST API uses a manually generated personal Bearer token available on paid organization plans, not delegated third-party OAuth. The unscoped token follows all data and broad mutation authority visible to its owning user, so Relay requires explicit approval of a separate customer-owned token product.

blocked.label: Connect through delegated OAuth
blocked.description: Missive does not document third-party client registration, authorization-code consent, granular scopes, refresh tokens, or per-installation revocation.

blocked.label: Use a personal API token
blocked.description: The manually generated token belongs to one paid-plan user and follows all resources and mutation authority visible to that user without granular scopes.

blocked.label: Use webhooks or custom channels
blocked.description: Webhook and custom-channel mechanisms have different event, content-injection, signing, retry, and lifecycle boundaries and are not a delegated account connection.

blocked.label: Access Missive data
blocked.description: Organizations, teams, users, accounts, conversations, messages, comments, drafts, posts, contacts, labels, tasks, responses, hooks, analytics, exports, and every read or write remain unavailable.

approvalProfiles.label: Unavailable
approvalProfiles.description: No agent action can be enabled until Relay approves a separately governed customer-owned API-token product or Missive publishes delegated OAuth.

runtimeSupport.description: No approved Missive credential, authority, or wrapper contract is available to mount as OpenClaw tools.
No approved Missive credential, authority, or wrapper contract is available to mount as Hermes tools.

providerSetup.blocker: Missive documents a broad customer-owned personal API token on paid organization plans, not granular delegated OAuth; changing the approved credential ownership model requires a product/security decision.
providerSetup.nextAction: Do not request a Missive token or show Connect. Reconsider after explicit approval of a narrowly governed user-owned token integration, or after Missive provides an official multi-tenant delegated OAuth and revocation contract.

evidence.supports: Missive instructs users to create a personal API token in preferences, requires a Productive-plan organization, and authenticates it as a Bearer token.

The same token accesses user-visible conversations and broad analytics, contact, message, draft, post, task, label, team, hook, and conversation-state read/write surfaces without documented token scopes.
Missive publishes API concurrency and rate limits but no delegated consent, refresh, or per-installation revocation lifecycle.
Missive webhooks are a separately configured event mechanism with message-content, optional signing, and retry behavior rather than delegated OAuth.
